record.original_question: For each t >= 5, what is the maximum spectral radius among all F_t-free graphs with m edges, and which extremal graphs attain that value, where F_t = K_1 \/ P_{t-1} is the fan graph on t vertices?

evidence.quote: Problem 9 (Zhang and Wang [46]). What is the maximum spectral radius and what are the corresponding extremal graphs among all Ft-free graphs with size m for t >= 5?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer t ≥ 2, let the fan graph F_t be the graph on t vertices defined as F_t = K_1 ∨ P_{t-1}, i.e., the join of a single vertex with a path on t-1 vertices. A simple graph G is called F_t-free if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to F_t. The spectral radius λ(G) of G is the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix.

For each integer t ≥ 5, determine the maximum value of λ(G) over all F_t-free simple graphs G with exactly m edges, and characterize all extremal graphs attaining this maximum.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is partially solved. The case t = 5 (gem-related) was settled by Zhang and Wang (2024) for odd m, and the case t = 6 was resolved for m ≥ 88 in arXiv:2412.13792. More general results for t = 2k+1 and t = 2k+2 with m sufficiently large appear in recent works (e.g., arXiv:2409.15918, published in J. Graph Theory 2025), giving λ(G) ≤ (k-1+√(4m-k²+1))/2 with equality for K_k ∨ ((m/k - (k-1)/2)K_1). However, the full problem for all t ≥ 5 and all m is not completely resolved.

status_evidence.title: Spectral radius of graphs of given size with a forbidden fan graph F6
status_evidence.snippet: The maximum spectral radius of F_6-free graphs with size m ≥ 88 was determined, along with the extremal graph.
status_evidence.claim: Case t=6 solved for sufficiently large m.

status_evidence.title: Spectral extrema of graphs with fixed size: forbidden a fan graph, friendship graph or theta graph
status_evidence.snippet: For k ≥ 2 and m sufficiently large, if G is F_{2k+1}-free or F_{2k+2}-free, then λ(G) ≤ (k-1+√(4m-k²+1))/2 with equality iff G ≅ K_k ∨ ((m/k - (k-1)/2)K_1).
status_evidence.claim: General t resolved for sufficiently large m, but not all m.

status_evidence.title: Spectral extremal graphs for fan graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Spectral extremal results for fan graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Related progress on the fan-graph extremal problem.
